seacow-cyberbase.name: SEACOW(r) Cyberbase Structure
seacow-cyberbase.description: Rule pack for SEACOW(r) framework: System, Entity, Activities (Capture, Output, Work, relation). Syncs tags to folders while preserving the knowledge organization meta-framework.
seacow-cyberbase.author: Cybersader

rules.name: CAPTURE: Clip folder sync
rules.description: Sync -clip/ tags to Capture/Clips folder structure (max 2 levels)

rules.name: CAPTURE: Inbox flat tag
rules.description: Sync -inbox flat tag to Capture/Inbox folder

rules.name: ENTITY: Cybersader work structure
rules.description: Sync --cybersader/ tags to Entity/Cybersader folder (Work activities)

rules.name: OUTPUT: Public Taxonomy structure
rules.description: Sync _publicTaxonomy/ tags to Output/Public folder (deep nesting allowed)

rules.name: OUTPUT: Main public facing (_/)
rules.description: Sync _/ tags (main public taxonomy) to Output/Main folder

rules.name: SYSTEM: Templates and config
rules.description: Sync /templates and /obsidian tags to System folder

notes: - C (Capture): Getting knowledge into the system (max 2-level nesting)
- O (Output): Interfacing knowledge to external systems (deep nesting allowed)
- W (Work): Deriving utility or processing knowledge
- r (relation): Interlinking knowledge (flat tags for cross-linking)
- Plain words (e.g., #research, #idea) = RELATION (not included in these rules - they remain as flat keyword tags)
- CAPTURE tags process first (most important for quick capture workflow)
- Entity/Work tags process next (personal knowledge work)
- OUTPUT tags process after (polished, structured content)
RELATION tags (plain keyword tags like #research, #idea) are intentionally NOT included in this rule pack.
They remain flat and are used for cross-linking across the vault without triggering folder moves.

seacow-templates.name: SEACOW(r) templates — multi-axis nested
seacow-templates.description: Template-shaped pack for SEACOW(r) framework vaults with multi-axis composition: per-entity scoping, Capture/Output/System axes, JD numbering inside Output, daily notes. Demonstrates nested implementations — rules compose so a path like Entity/User/Output/01 - Projects/X.md can match the more-specific Entity+Output+JD rule. All rules ship disabled.
seacow-templates.author: Cybersader

rules.name: Capture: clips (web clippings)
rules.description: Capture/Clips/{deeper...} ↔ #-clip/{deeper...}

rules.name: Capture: inbox (marker-only, lossy)
rules.description: Capture/Inbox/{discarded...} ↔ #-inbox — flat marker, deeper structure discarded going to tag. Recommend frontmatterMemory: true for inverse recovery.

rules.name: Entity: per-user namespace
rules.description: Entity/{owner}/{deeper...} ↔ #--{owner | kebab-case}/{deeper...}

rules.name: Entity + Output + JD nested (multi-axis composition)
rules.description: Entity/{owner}/Output/{num:\d{1,2}} - {area}/{deeper...} ↔ #--{owner}/{num}-{area}/{deeper...}. Higher specificity wins over the entity-scope rule for matching paths.

rules.name: Output: public taxonomy
rules.description: Output/Public/{topic}/{deeper...} ↔ #_/{topic | kebab-case}/{deeper...}

rules.name: Output: main (private)
rules.description: Output/Main/{deeper...} ↔ #_main/{deeper...}

rules.name: Daily notes (relation tag)
rules.description: 🕸️ Daily Notes/{deeper...} ↔ #daily/{deeper...}

notes: All 7 rules ship DISABLED. Review and enable individually.

Multi-axis composition: when a path matches MULTIPLE rules (e.g., Entity/User/Output/01 - Projects/X), the more-specific rule wins via specificity-aware matching (lower priority number for tighter slot count).
Entity scoping (rule 3) is the catch-all for any Entity/{owner} subpath; Entity+Output+JD (rule 4) is more specific and overrides for matching paths.
Tag prefixes follow SEACOW(r) conventions: #- = capture, #-- = entity, #_ = output, # plain = relation. See github.com/cybersader/seacowr-knowledge-platform-meta-framework for the full vocabulary.
Capture/Inbox uses frontmatterMemory: true so the inverse direction can recover the original Inbox folder name despite the marker-only collapse.

templates-demo.name: Path Lens templates — demo
templates-demo.description: Demonstration pack showing each Path Lens shape — identity, glob, filters, and convention-tolerant variants for emoji-prefixed and Johnny-Decimal-prefixed folder names. Use as a copy-paste reference when authoring template-shaped rules.
templates-demo.author: Cybersader

establish.summary: Three folders demonstrating identity (Projects), filter chain (Areas with kebab-case), and marker-only-via-glob (Capture/Inbox).

rules.name: Projects: identity round-trip
rules.description: Projects/{topic} ↔ #projects/{topic} — total bijection, single-segment slot

rules.name: Areas: kebab-case filter on tag side
rules.description: Areas/{area} ↔ #areas/{area | kebab-case} — conditional bijection (round-trips for clean inputs)

rules.name: Projects: glob slot for arbitrary depth
rules.description: Projects/{topic}/{deeper...} ↔ #projects/{topic}/{deeper...} — glob slot preserves structure

rules.name: Inbox: marker-only via discarded glob
rules.description: Capture/Inbox/{discarded...} ↔ #-inbox — provably lossy (folder-only slot). Recoverable per-file via F3 frontmatter witness.

rules.name: Emoji-prefixed PARA: 📁 Projects
rules.description: 📁 Projects/{topic} ↔ #projects/{topic} — total bijection, literal emoji prefix in the template means the rule fires only on emoji-prefixed folders. Author the template to match your folder convention; no normalization magic needed.

rules.name: Johnny Decimal + emoji: 📁 01 - Projects
rules.description: 📁 01 - Projects/{topic} ↔ #projects/{topic} — emoji + JD prefix in the literal; slot only captures the topic. The JD number itself is part of the literal match (not captured as a slot), so it must be authored verbatim. For users with stable JD numbering this is the simplest move.

notes: This pack ships 6 template rules — only the first 2 are enabled by default. Enable rules 3-6 manually to experiment.
Rule 1 (identity): green chip — round-trips perfectly. Use as a starting template.
Rule 2 (kebab-case filter): yellow chip — conditional. Round-trips for inputs that are already lowercase-with-hyphens.
Rule 3 (glob slot): green chip — round-trips when both sides use glob.
Rule 4 (marker-only): orange chip — lossy by design. Multiple inbox files collapse to one tag. Per-file recovery requires F3 (frontmatter witness, future).
Rule 5 (emoji-prefixed PARA): green chip. Matches '📁 Projects/Web Auth' style folders directly via literal emoji in the template. Copy + adjust the emoji + folder name for your own convention.
Rule 6 (JD + emoji): green chip. Matches '📁 01 - Projects/Web Auth'. The JD number is part of the literal — for stable numbering only. Dynamic JD numbers would need a future {jd-number}-style slot.
